lines: An eight-step chord sequencer: every step carries a root, a chord type, an inversion and a length in clock beats, and the chord leaves as four separate pitches and as one polyphonic cable
Sets how many of the eight steps the sequence runs through, 1 to 8
Sets the root note of that step, in semitones from C0 up to B6, and the display for that step names it
Sets the chord type for that step: major, minor, major 7th, dominant 7th, minor 7th, suspended 4th, suspended 2nd, diminished or augmented
Chooses the bass note of that step's chord, 0 to 3, by lifting every note below the chosen one up an octave
Sets how many clock beats that step lasts, 1 to 16, and at 0 the step is skipped altogether
Advances the sequence on each rising edge; a step lasts for as many edges as its Length knob sets
A rising edge returns the sequence to step 1 and restarts the beat count within that step
Adds to the number of steps set by the Steps knob, one step per volt, with the total held between 1 and 8
Adds to the length of that step, one clock beat per volt, with the total held between 0 and 16
The root of the current chord as a 1V/octave pitch, whatever the inversion
The third of the current chord as a 1V/octave pitch, whatever the inversion
The fifth of the current chord as a 1V/octave pitch, whatever the inversion
The seventh of the current chord as a 1V/octave pitch; on a chord with no seventh it repeats the root
Every note of the current chord on one polyphonic cable, three channels for a triad and four where the chord has a seventh
Carries 10V through the step and a 5V pulse lasting almost one beat on its final beat, with one channel per note of the chord
A 1ms pulse at 10V on the first step of each new pass through the sequence
Note — the eight chord readouts are drawn artwork rather than controls, so no help note is reached by clicking one
Note — the sequence does not move until a clock is patched to the clock input; every step change, gate and end-of-cycle pulse is made on a rising edge there
Progress.notes: The README lists the chord types with sus2 before sus4; the code and the readout put sus4 first, at knob position 5, with sus2 at 6. The README also calls the Gate output polyphonic 'for each step of the sequence': in the code every channel of it carries the same gate, and the channel count follows the number of notes in the chord.

lines: An arpeggiator driven by a polyphonic keyboard: the notes whose gates are high make up the sequence, and one of them is played on each clock
Chooses the order the notes play in: Up, Down, Inclusive up and back with the end notes twice, Exclusive up and back with them once, Outside In from both ends inwards, Order as played, or Random
Sets the length of the output gate as a fraction of the measured clock interval, 0 to 1, with a floor of 1ms
Sets how many octaves the sequence spans, 1 to 4, each octave repeating the held notes a volt higher
Holds the notes in the sequence after the keys are released, and clears them when a new note arrives after every key has been let go
Adds to the pattern chosen by the knob, one pattern per volt, with the total held between 1 and 7
Adds to the gate length set by the knob, a whole clock interval per volt, with the total held between 0 and 1
Adds to the octave span set by the knob, one octave per volt, with the total held between 1 and 4
Advances the sequence by one note on each rising edge, and the time between edges sets the gate length
A rising edge returns the sequence to its first note
The polyphonic pitches the sequence is built from; a channel joins the sequence only while its gate channel is high
The polyphonic gates saying which of the incoming pitches belong to the sequence; with every gate low and Latch off, the sequence returns to its first note
A 5V gate at each step, lasting the fraction of the clock interval set by the Gate knob
The pitch of the current step, 1V per octave
Note — nothing comes out until a clock is patched to the clock input and a polyphonic keyboard is patched to both the pitch and the gate inputs; a step is taken only on a clock edge
Note — a note joins the sequence only while its gate channel is high, so with every gate low and Latch off the outputs stay at 0V
Menu — Polyphonic output — moves each step on to the next of sixteen channels on both outputs, so a long envelope on one step is not cut off by the next
Arp.notes: Input index 3 is Reset and index 4 is Clock, which is the reverse of the panel order inside the In box. Bypassing the module passes the v/oct input to the v/oct output and the gate input to the gate output.
